title: The Births of John and Jesus
summary: In Herod's days the priest Zacharias is told by the angel Gabriel in the temple that his wife Elisabeth, barren and old, will bear John, and he is struck dumb for doubting. Gabriel then tells Mary in Nazareth she will conceive the Son of the Highest; she answers, 'Behold the handmaid of the Lord,' and visits Elisabeth. John is born, and Zacharias names him. Joseph and Mary go to Bethlehem for the enrollment, where Jesus is born and laid in a manger, and angels announce him to shepherds.

title: Presentation and the Boy Jesus in the Temple
summary: At eight days Jesus is circumcised, and Mary and Joseph bring him to Jerusalem to be presented and to offer a pair of turtledoves. Simeon, told he would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ, takes the child in his arms and calls him a light to the Gentiles and a sign that will be spoken against; Anna the prophetess also gives thanks. At twelve, Jesus stays behind in Jerusalem, and his parents find him after three days in the temple among the teachers.

title: Rejection at Nazareth
summary: Jesus returns to Galilee in the power of the Spirit. In the Nazareth synagogue he reads from Isaiah, 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me,' about good news for the poor and release for captives, and says the scripture is fulfilled in their hearing. He adds that no prophet is accepted in his own country, citing Elias and the widow of Sarepta and Eliseus and Naaman. The congregation, filled with wrath, drives him out and tries to throw him off a cliff, but he passes through them.

title: The Miraculous Catch
summary: Standing by the lake of Gennesaret as the crowd presses to hear him, Jesus gets into Simon's boat and teaches from it. Afterward he tells Simon to launch out and let down the nets; Simon says they have toiled all night and caught nothing, but obeys, and the nets break with the number of fish. Simon falls at Jesus' knees, saying 'Depart from me; for I am a sinful man.' Jesus tells him not to fear, since he will catch men, and Simon, James and John leave everything and follow him.

title: The Centurion and the Widow's Son
summary: In Capernaum a centurion whose valued servant is sick sends Jewish elders, who say he loves the nation and built them a synagogue. As Jesus nears the house, the centurion sends friends to say he is not worthy to have him under his roof and that Jesus need only speak the word; Jesus marvels at such faith and the servant is found well. The next day at the gate of Nain Jesus meets a funeral for a widow's only son, touches the bier and says 'Young man, arise'; the son sits up and speaks.

title: The Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus
summary: A Pharisee named Simon invites Jesus to eat, and a woman of the city, known as a sinner, brings an alabaster box of ointment, stands behind him weeping, wets his feet with tears, wipes them with her hair and anoints them. Simon thinks a prophet would know what kind of woman she is. Jesus tells of two debtors forgiven different amounts, asks which will love more, and contrasts Simon's lack of hospitality with her actions. He tells her that her sins are forgiven.

title: The Good Samaritan and Mary and Martha
summary: A lawyer tests Jesus by asking what he must do to inherit eternal life, and answers that the law says to love God and one's neighbor; wishing to justify himself, he asks who his neighbor is. Jesus tells of a man beaten by robbers, passed by a priest and a Levite, and helped by a Samaritan who pays for his care, and says, 'Go, and do thou likewise.' At a village Martha serves while her sister Mary sits at Jesus' feet, and Jesus says Mary has chosen the good part.

title: The Lost Sheep, Coin and Son
summary: Publicans and sinners draw near to hear Jesus, and the Pharisees and scribes murmur. He tells of a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one and a woman who searches for a lost coin, each ending in rejoicing. In the third parable a younger son wastes his inheritance in a far country and returns hoping to be a hired servant; the father runs to embrace him and holds a feast. The elder brother is angry, and the father pleads with him. The parable ends without saying whether he comes in.

title: The Rich Man and Lazarus
summary: Jesus tells of a rich man in purple and fine linen who feasts daily while a beggar named Lazarus, covered with sores, lies at his gate. Both die; Lazarus is carried by angels to Abraham's bosom, and the rich man is in torment. He asks for water, but Abraham says a great gulf is fixed between them. He asks that Lazarus warn his five brothers, and Abraham answers that they have Moses and the prophets; if they will not hear them, they will not be persuaded though one rose from the dead.

title: Zacchaeus
summary: In Jericho Zacchaeus, chief among the publicans and rich, is small and climbs a sycomore tree to see Jesus pass. Jesus looks up and says he must stay at his house that day, and Zacchaeus comes down and receives him joyfully, while the crowd murmurs that he has gone to a sinner's house. Zacchaeus says he will give half his goods to the poor and restore fourfold anything taken by false accusation. Jesus says salvation has come to this house and that the Son of man came to seek and save the lost.

title: The Road to Emmaus
summary: On the day of the resurrection two disciples walk to Emmaus, talking of the crucifixion, when Jesus joins them but they do not recognize him. One, Cleopas, tells him of Jesus of Nazareth, their hope that he would redeem Israel, and the women's report of an empty tomb. Jesus explains the scriptures concerning himself from Moses and the prophets. They urge him to stay, and when he breaks bread their eyes are opened and he vanishes. They return to Jerusalem to tell the eleven.

title: The Ascension
summary: While the two disciples tell what happened, Jesus stands among the eleven and says 'Peace be unto you.' They are terrified, thinking him a spirit, and he shows his hands and feet and eats a piece of broiled fish. He opens their understanding of the scriptures, says repentance and remission of sins will be preached to all nations beginning at Jerusalem, and tells them to wait for power from on high. At Bethany he blesses them and is carried up into heaven; they return with great joy.
